result:
I graded Riley's submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | Riley picked the loop as what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley said the model opens the booking system itself. The model only outputs a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | Riley chose a step limit as the safeguard against a looping agent. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1 and said the model "runs the 3 tools itself". The correct count is 4 model calls. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is right but gives no reason. The model needs the result in its next input to pick its next step or answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Riley correctly said the model picks tools from their descriptions. Riley also claimed the model remembers earlier sessions on its own, which is wrong. |

**Summary for Riley:** You have the shape of the loop and know the model chooses tools from descriptions. The idea to fix is who does what. The model only writes text, either a tool request or the final answer. The program runs the tools, feeds results back and supplies any memory.

**Next step:** Redraw the laser cutter trace with two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and count the model calls.

I also added `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` for the open M4 and M3 misconceptions and updated `NOTES.md`. I did not grade `submissions/s2.json`, since you only asked for s1.

Do you want me to grade s2 next? It would show whether the misconceptions cleared after four days.
